title: Voting-based approach for differentially private federated learning

pse.problem: Gradient averaging based DPFL methods require costly communication rounds and hardly work with large capacity models due to explicit dimension dependence in its added noise
pse.solution_function: The system performs differentially private federated learning using a voting-based approach for labeling unlabeled data from two global servers. Each agent trains a local model using their private data, labels the data using the voting-based approach, and contributes to the training of a global model.
pse.solution_structure: The system includes memory and processors. Each agent has local data, a local model, and maintains a data-independent feature extractor. Two global servers are used for storing unlabeled data. A global model is trained using the labeled data generated by the agents.
pse.solution_implementation: The system first labels a subset of unlabeled data from the first global server using a voting-based DPFL computation where each agent trains their local model on their private data and contributes to the labeling. Next, it labels another subset of unlabeled data from the second global server using a similar voting-based DPFL computation with data-independent feature extractors. Finally, the system trains a global model using the labeled data generated by the agents to provide provable differential privacy for both instance-level and agent-level privacy regimes.
pse.effect: The method reduces communication rounds and enables working with large capacity models in federated learning while maintaining differential privacy guarantees
